qs.q: For the GGTA1 guide, what fraction of examined blastocysts had biallelic mutations in each of the four treatment groups?
qs.a: Single electroporation with zona pellucida intact 8/19 (42.1%); single with ZP removed 16/17 (94.1%); double with ZP intact 17/19 (89.5%); double with ZP removed 19/19 (100%)

qs.q: What were the electroporation conditions and when was electroporation done in the single and double treatments?
qs.a: Five 1 ms pulses at 25 V with 100 ng/ul of each gRNA and 200 ng/ul Cas9 protein. Single: 10 h after IVF starts. Double: immediately before IVF and again 10 h after IVF starts

qs.q: Did double electroporation or zona pellucida removal improve editing of the CMAH gene?
qs.a: No. All examined blastocysts were mutated in every group and biallelic rates were already above 80% (81.3% to 95.0%); neither treatment had a significant effect. The authors say single electroporation was already highly efficient

qs.q: For GGTA1, did zona pellucida removal significantly help in both the single and the double electroporation groups?
qs.a: No. ZP removal significantly increased mutation efficiency in the single electroporation group (p<0.009) but not in the double electroporation group; double electroporation raised total and biallelic rates in ZP-intact zygotes (p<0.046) but not in ZP-free ones, which were already at or near 100%

qs.q: For B4GALNT2, did the treatments change blastocyst formation, and what do the numbers show?
qs.a: The paper reports no effect on blastocyst formation rates. Numerically the double electroporation ZP-free group was lowest (7.4%) against 11.5% for single ZP-intact, with only 198 to 233 oocytes per group and no significant difference reported

qs.q: What limitations do the authors acknowledge?
qs.a: Fertilization rate and polyspermy not evaluated; small groups and sequencing failures; TIDE on Sanger data may miss complex or low-frequency mosaic alleles; no off-target analysis; outcomes only to blastocyst stage; mosaicism inferred from whole-blastocyst sequencing, not single cells; embryo quality judged only by blastocyst rate (no cell counts or apoptosis)

qs.q: Does the study show that the edited embryos develop into healthy pigs?
qs.a: No. Outcomes were assessed only up to the blastocyst stage; no embryo transfer or offspring were produced, which the authors list as future work

qs.q: Do the authors attribute the improved editing to the timing of electroporation alone?
qs.a: No. They argue timing alone is unlikely to explain it (their earlier work found comparable rates for pre-IVF and post-IVF electroporation); they attribute it to the combined effect of repeated electroporation and timing, and say mechanisms for gene-dependent differences remain unclear

qs.q: What was the off-target mutation rate of the editing?
qs.a: NOT STATED. Off-target analyses were not performed

qs.q: How many piglets were born from the edited embryos?
qs.a: NOT STATED. No embryo transfer or births are reported
